title: Short Stuff: The Disappearance of Ambrose Bierce
summary: Short Stuff episode on the 1913 disappearance of Civil War veteran writer Ambrose Bierce, who vanished in Mexico after leaving California to join or meet Pancho Villa. The hosts cover his life and works (The Devil's Dictionary, "An Occurrence at Owl Creek Bridge"), the last letter postmarked Chihuahua, and competing theories: execution by firing squad by Villa or federal troops, a claimed dinner with Villa, dying of pneumonia in Marfa, Texas, and suicide at the Grand Canyon. They also mention Don Swaim's biography and the film Old Gringo.

segments.title: Who was Ambrose Bierce
segments.summary: Hosts introduce Ambrose Bierce as a journalist and horror writer born in Ohio in 1842, a Civil War veteran, author of The Devil's Dictionary and 'An Occurrence at Owl Creek Bridge.' They note he never became a novelist and was bitter about it, and mention Don Swaim's book on him.
topics: An Occurrence at Owl Creek Bridge

segments.title: Disappearance and early theories
segments.summary: Bierce vanished in December 1913 after leaving California for Mexico, supposedly to find Pancho Villa. Hosts outline the Grand Canyon suicide idea and the main story that he went to ride with Villa.

segments.title: Break
segments.summary: Brief ad break before the discussion continues.

segments.title: Last letter from Chihuahua
segments.summary: Bierce's last known letter was postmarked from Chihuahua, Mexico, and reportedly says he hopes to be shot against a Mexican wall. Hosts discuss skeptics who doubt the letter or think someone mailed it for him.

segments.title: Competing death theories
segments.summary: Theories include execution by firing squad (priest James Lenert's account in Sierra Mojada), a claimed dinner in which Villa admitted killing Bierce after he insulted him (from Adolf Danziger de Castro), and a Marfa, Texas pneumonia death reported by Jake Silverstein.

segments.title: Fiction, film and sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts note the Grand Canyon suicide theory and Bierce's son's suicide, mention the fictional love story ending in Swaim's book and the film Old Gringo, and invite listener messages.
